criteria: CRITERIA.md — pre-registered before any pair was selected
annotation: SINGLE-ANNOTATED. One annotator. No inter-annotator agreement was measured and none is claimed.
purpose: Go/no-go evidence for A1 embedding-based mismatch detection.

fields.assertion: what the draft claims, as a lawyer would write it
fields.statute: canonical statute name as the corpus spells it
fields.section: section or article number as cited
fields.label: supported | misgrounded_gross | misgrounded_same_topic | fabricated | repealed | omitted
fields.source: logged = taken verbatim from this system's own recorded answers; synthetic = written for this set
fields.real_heading: the actual heading of the cited section, from the corpus
fields.correct_section: for misgrounded pairs, the provision that should have been cited
fields.rule: which CRITERIA.md rule assigned the label
fields.known_gap: true when the current verifier is expected to MISS this

pairs.label: supported

pairs.label: supported

pairs.assertion: This section fixes the limitation period for appeals to a High Court.

pairs.assertion: This provision sets out the punishment for theft under Pakistani criminal law.
pairs.label: misgrounded_gross
pairs.rule: rule 1 — different statute, procedural court-constitution vs substantive offence

It is NOT drawn from the logs: the seven recorded s.302 mentions all read 'PPC Section 302 is not applicable here', i.e. the model correctly rejecting it. An earlier claim that this was a logged fabrication was wrong and has been corrected in citation_grounding.py.

pairs.assertion: A landlord may evict a tenant without notice under this provision.

pairs.rule: rule 2

pairs.assertion: Oral evidence in a criminal trial must be direct and cannot be hearsay.
pairs.label: misgrounded_gross

pairs.note: FAILURE_CASE_001. The recorded answer rendered it flatly as 'PPC Section 382 — Theft'. s.382 is an aggravated form carrying a far heavier sentence; s.379 is the general punishment section.

pairs.assertion: Theft of movable property from a person's dwelling attracts the ordinary punishment for theft under this section.

pairs.assertion: This section defines the offence of criminal breach of trust by a public servant.

pairs.assertion: A police officer may investigate a cognizable case without the order of a Magistrate under this section.

pairs.assertion: This provision governs criminal trespass committed by night in order to commit an offence.

pairs.assertion: This provision confers original jurisdiction on the High Court to enforce fundamental rights.
pairs.label: misgrounded_same_topic

pairs.known_gap_reason: PPC marks omissions as footnotes ('The following was omitted by A.O. 1961, Art. 2 and Sch.') attached to the section, not as range declarations. The current parser reads only range and single-line declarations, so it will report this VERIFIED. Recorded as a measured limit, not a verifier failure.
